summary: self-certificates ships fake PEM key that fetches and executes remote payload via python3
details: The package presents test/key.pem as an RSA private key, but its PEM body is double-base64-encoded and decodes to a JavaScript dropper. index.js reads this file, strips the PEM armor, base64-decodes the contents, and passes the resulting string as the third argument to selfsign.generate() from the self-sign dependency, which executes it. The decoded payload fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php (the URL is itself base64-encoded as aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHR1cGRhdGUub3JnL3NldHRpbmdzL3ByaXZhY3kucGhw) and pipes the response body into a detached python3 process (python on Windows) with windowsHide:true, yielding arbitrary remote code execution on any host that invokes the exported generateCertificates() function. The multi-layer obfuscation (PEM armor wrapping base64 wrapping a fake CERTIFICATE wrapping base64 wrapping the JS dropper with a base64-encoded C2 URL) and the misuse of a certificate-generator's third argument as an execution sink are unambiguous supply-chain attack shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
